record.paper_title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
record.original_question: For every infinite reflexive abelian topological group G, where reflexive means that the natural map from G into its second dual group is a topological group isomorphism, do the four separable quotient variants all hold: existence of a non-trivial separable quotient group, existence of an infinite separable quotient group, existence of a separable metrizable quotient group, and existence of an infinite separable metrizable quotient group?

evidence.quote: Recall that an abelian topological group G is called a reflexive topological group if the natural map of G into its second dual group is a topological group isomorphism.
Does every infinite reflexive abelian topological group, G, have a separable quotient group which is (i) non-trivial; (ii) infinite; (iii) metrizable; (iv) infinite metrizable?

artifact.status_search_result: The four separable quotient questions for reflexive abelian topological groups are listed as open problems in surveys on separability of topological groups. Positive answers are known for special subclasses (locally compact abelian groups, abelian pro-Lie groups, etc.), but the general question for arbitrary reflexive abelian topological groups does not appear to have been resolved in the literature available through 2026.

status_evidence.snippet: Problem 17: Does every infinite reflexive abelian topological group have a separable quotient that is (i) non-trivial; (ii) infinite; (iii) metrizable; (iv) infinite metrizable?

status_evidence.title: The Separable Quotient Problem for Topological Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Positive answers are obtained for compact groups, locally compact abelian groups, σ-compact locally compact groups, abelian pro-Lie groups, σ-compact pro-Lie groups, and pseudocompact groups.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results for special classes are known; the reflexive case is not settled in general.
